text:
brian: CI perf job for release v1.23 flagged a 15% p95 decode slowdown on shortseq after the midnight merge, linking logs: https://ci.internal/reports/70678
carla: saw that, grabbing flamegraphs now. quick grep shows more time in 'kv_prefetch_worker' and memcpy on the decode hotpath
alice: oof. does this reproduce locally with the nightly artifact?
brian: yes on a g4dn-like node. repro script: `./tests/perf/run_decode_bench --model redwood-small --seq 32 --concurrency 8 --artifact=nightly-7067`
carla: attaching snippet of perf top output:
```
  42.3%  runtime  [kernel] kv_prefetch_worker
  18.1%  runtime  libcuda.so memcpy
  12.5%  runtime  attention_fused_forward
  6.8%   runtime  decode_dispatcher
```
omar: interesting that fused attention shows some of it — could be the reorder introduced in PR #4123?
brian: PR 4123 did the fused-op reordering and touched kernel selector heuristics. suspecting a steer to the matmul-transpose path on short sequences
carla: i ran a small bisect across merges between 7060000..7067800. the p95 jumps right after commit `a1b2c3d` (merge of PR 4123).
perf-bot: CI Perf Alert: job perf/decode-shortseq failed p95 threshold at 2026-03-20T02:10:12Z (link: https://ci.internal/70678/perf) :warning:
alice: can someone try forcing kernel-selector back to previous policy and test? a quick canary could confirm
omar: patched a dev build to set `KERNEL_SELECTOR_POLICY=legacy_shortseq` and ran the bench — p95 returned to baseline (15% improvement).
brian: ok that's a smoking gun. what's different in selector? I see change where we prefer fused-transpose when batch<16 to avoid extra allocs
carla: the fused-transpose path triggers extra KV memcpy because of a temp buffer layout mismatch; for shortseq the memcpy cost dominates. i have a minimal repro that prints memcpy sizes: `printf("memcpy bytes=%zu\n", bytes)` -> shows frequent ~1.2MB copies
alice: is there a low-risk revert we can do for the policy switch in the rollout? or a targeted fix to avoid the memcpy for shortseq
omar: quick patch: if seq<=64 and batch<=8 prefer legacy matmul path. i can open a hotfix PR and run CI canary
brian: please do. also add a short unit test comparing token latency across both policies so we don't regress again silently
carla: logging suggestion: add a selector debug metric `selector.choice` tag for shortseq, emit to traces — will help postmortem
perf-bot: Canary run started for hotfix PR #4189 (job: perf/canary-decode-shortseq)
alice: if canary passes, let's pin rollout to 10% then 100% after 1 hour; i'll schedule the rollout window
omar: pushing PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4189. diff swaps policy ordering under shortseq guard and adds the selector metric
brian: big thanks. follow up: run the `kv_cache_throughput` microbench against on-host NVMe to ensure we didn't accidentally change eviction timings
carla: noted. i'll run kv benchmarks and post numbers in this thread in ~30m
brian: also add a short note to the release notes about the kernel-selector change and the perf threshold gap so customers know we observed the spike
alice: good call. if canary fails, we'll revert commit `a1b2c3d` and open an incident page. keep me updated
carla: results: kv benchmark unchanged. canary perf job passed. rolling out 10% now :thumbsup:
brian: monitoring p95 traces — looks stable so far. will keep an eye during next hour
carla: adding trace screenshot to the ticket and include `selector.choice` tags. baseline p95 = 46ms, hotfix p95=45ms (noise), pre-fix = 54ms
omar: merging hotfix PR in 2m after CI green
brian: thanks team. postmortem TODOs: 1) add selector unit tests 2) add perf gate in CI for shortseq p95 3) retro on why fuse reordering lacked shortseq perf test
alice: put the TODOs in the release retro doc and assign owners. closing thread once rollout at 100%
perf-bot: Canary complete. rollout status: 10% -> healthy. Next step: 100% in 1h if stable.
